item.title: Recent Advances in Optimization and Decision Making under Uncertainty: Theory and Algorithms
item.content:encoded:
Abdel Lisser, Paris-Saclay University

Jia Liu, Xi'an Jiaotong University

Francesca Maggioni, University of Bergamo

S. K. Neogy, Indian Statistical Institute

Vikas Vikram Singh, Indian Institute of Technology Delhi

This special issue invites theoretical and methodological contributions advancing optimization and decision-making under uncertainty. It seeks original research developing new optimization models, analytical results, computational methods, and convergence theories across mathematical optimization, stochastic optimization, robust optimization, game theory, and sequential decision-making.

The special issue is organized in conjunction with the International Conference on Operations Research: Theory, Applications and Emerging Technologies (ICORSI 2026) at Indian Institute of Technology Delhi. However, submissions are welcomed from all researchers in these areas regardless of conference participation, and all papers will undergo standard peer review.

Appel publié par Annals of Operations Research. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Mathematical programming
  • Convex, nonconvex, and mixed-integer optimization
  • Stochastic, robust, and distributionally robust optimization
  • Chance-constrained optimization
  • Variational inequalities and equilibrium problems
  • Game theory and multi-agent optimization
  • Markov decision processes and stochastic games
  • Reinforcement learning for sequential decision making
  • Online and data-driven optimization
  • Optimization under risk measures
  • Bayesian optimization
  • Black-box optimization

Timeline

  • March 31, 2028: Submission deadline

item.title: Advanced Machine Learning for System Reliability Management
item.content:encoded:
Yan-Fu Li, Tsinghua University

Hoang Pham, Rutgers University

Xu-Feng Zhao, Nanjing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics

Industrial systems produce vast sensor-generated datasets that strain computational resources. Advanced machine learning techniques including transfer learning, federated learning, quantum machine learning, and reinforcement learning provide scalable solutions for handling large data volumes and enabling informed decision-making. Recent applications of these techniques to system reliability management encompass fault diagnosis, health assessment, remaining useful life prediction, degradation analysis, and maintenance optimization. This special issue seeks original research papers, reviews, and case studies exploring these emerging applications.

Appel publié par Annals of Operations Research. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Deep learning for anomaly detection and/or fault detection
  • Machine learning-enhanced maintenance optimization
  • Federated learning for system monitoring and predictive maintenance
  • Reinforcement learning for maintenance decision making
  • Transfer learning for cross-domain maintenance
  • Generative models for synthetic data generation for predictive maintenance
  • Self-supervised learning for unlabeled data for fault detection
  • Large models for fault detection and/or diagnosis
  • Generative models for reliability testing
  • Meta-heuristics for large-scale reliability design optimization

Timeline

  • September 30, 2026: Submission deadline

While the special issue originates from the Workshop on Quantitative Finance 2026 held in Bergamo, it welcomes submissions from all researchers in the area, not limited to workshop participants.

item.title: Advances in Reliability and Statistical Computing for Intelligent Systems
item.content:encoded:
Hoang Pham, Rutgers University

This special issue addresses the growing importance of reliability and statistical computing in AI-driven intelligent systems deployed across everyday applications and the service industry. The focus is on developing methods that enable these systems to deliver dependable and timely responses in real-world settings.

The issue seeks papers presenting novel theoretical research and practical methods in advanced reliability and statistical computing for intelligent systems. Submissions with applications to real-world problems are particularly encouraged, spanning areas such as robotics, medical care, education, surveillance, and transportation.

item.title: Climate Transition and Operational Risk Modelling: Implications for Supply Chains and Financial Decision-Making
item.content:encoded:
Andrea Flori, Politecnico di Milano

Anna Maria Gambaro, Università del Piemonte Orientale

Ioannis Kyriakou, University of London

Duc Khuong Nguyen, EMLV Business School

Climate-related risks threaten financial and economic systems through their effects on supply chains and firm operations. The transition to a low-carbon economy creates substantial uncertainty, particularly regarding timing and pace, destabilizing carbon-intensive sectors and triggering systemic challenges. This necessitates rigorous analytical methods to quantify climate risks and understand their propagation through interconnected economic systems.

Firms face tension between short-term profitability and long-term sustainability when transitioning to low-carbon operations. Supply chain vulnerabilities persist through global production networks where disruptions propagate, and financial markets transmit climate risks via asset prices and liquidity channels. This special issue welcomes operations research contributions using robust optimization, machine learning, and innovative analytical techniques to address how financial institutions and firms manage climate transition risks in portfolios and supply chains.

item.title: Collaborative Intelligence in Operations Research: Models, Methods, and Applications
item.content:encoded:
Olga Battaïa, Kedge Business School

Yasser Dessouky, San Jose State University

Reza Zanjirani Farahani, Paris School of Business

Masood Fathi, University of Skövde

Madjid Tavana, La Salle University

Modern operations research requires approaches combining human expertise with artificial intelligence and distributed problem-solving. This special issue addresses how collaborative intelligence—the synergy between human decision-makers, AI systems, and mathematical models—can enhance adaptability and efficiency in complex operational environments.

Traditional OR methods struggle with dynamic and uncertain decision-making. While AI offers computational power, autonomous systems face challenges with uncertainty and interpretability. Collaborative intelligence bridges this gap by leveraging human intuition alongside AI capabilities.

The special issue welcomes theoretical and applied research on collaborative, multi-agent, and adaptive decision-making frameworks that advance how human-AI partnership, multi-agent coordination, and data-driven learning enhance operations research methodologies.

item.title: Contextual Optimization with Side Information: Theory, Methodology, and Applications
item.content:encoded:
Stelios Bekiros, University of Turin

Andrea D'Ariano, Roma Tre University

Peng Wu, Fuzhou University

Guowei Zhang, Dalian University of Technology

Modern operations research integrates optimization with machine learning and statistics to incorporate side information—such as demand patterns and market conditions—into decision-making processes. This contextual optimization approach enables more adaptive and data-driven policies than classical optimization, though significant challenges persist including high-dimensional data, noisy observations, distribution shifts, and computational constraints.

The field requires new theories and frameworks that systematically combine learning and optimization under uncertainty, with emphasis on improving actual operational performance. This special issue invites high-quality contributions developing novel theories, models, algorithms, and applications addressing contextual decision-making using side information, spanning prescriptive analytics, adaptive algorithms, and real-world applications in transportation, supply chains, and healthcare.

item.title: Data-Driven Reliability Modeling and Decision Support in Industrial Engineering Systems
item.content:encoded:
Yi-Kuei Lin, National Yang Ming Chiao Tung University

This special issue seeks contributions on data-driven and intelligent approaches to reliability modeling for industrial engineering systems, including manufacturing, supply chains, logistics, energy, transportation, and service operations. The growing availability of operational and condition-monitoring data has created opportunities to complement traditional probabilistic and stochastic reliability methods with machine learning and statistical learning techniques.

The issue emphasizes the integration of reliability modeling with decision support frameworks, enabling practitioners to move beyond reliability assessment toward actionable, reliability-informed decisions under uncertainty. Both theoretical developments and practical applications are welcome, with particular interest in papers demonstrating methodological rigor and real-world industrial relevance.

item.title: Data Science
item.content:encoded:
Dries F. Benoit, Ghent University

Kristof Coussement, Institut d'Economie Scientifique Et de Gestion

Cem İyigün, Middle East Technical University

Asil Oztekin, University of Massachusetts Lowell

This special section seeks papers that advance both theoretical and practical contributions to data science and predictive analytics. The focus is on demonstrating how new techniques create organizational value and may require changes in business processes. The work bridges operations research with analytics, treating analytics as an organizational discipline that leverages both data science and OR methodologies.

The section invites researchers and practitioners to explore multiple dimensions of analytics: ethical and governance challenges in data collection and behavioral influence; applications and limitations of OR techniques with big data and distributed systems; organizational barriers to analytics adoption and real-time OR applications; methods for data quality, hypothesis testing, and integration of unstructured data; and how visualization and problem structuring enhance analytics projects.

item.title: Global Supply Chain Reconfiguration Under Tariff Uncertainty
item.content:encoded:
Jiaguo Liu, Dalian Maritime University

Hakan Yildiz, Wayne State University

Guoqing Zhang, University of Windsor

Global supply chains face mounting pressures from tariff uncertainty and shifting trade policies, requiring urgent reconfiguration of sourcing strategies, manufacturing locations, and logistics networks. The current environment presents unprecedented complexity with high tariff rates, retaliatory measures, and escalating trade tensions creating significant practical challenges.

This special issue seeks high-quality research applying Operations Research and Artificial Intelligence methods to address supply chain reconfiguration challenges under tariff uncertainty. The journal welcomes theoretical developments, methodological innovations, applied modeling studies, and interdisciplinary work integrating OR, AI, supply chain management, and international economics with real-world case applications.

item.title: Multiple Objective Programming and Goal Programming: Artificial Intelligence for Decision Making in Economic and Social Sciences
item.content:encoded:
Matteo Rocca, University of Insubria

Davide La Torre, Skema Business School

Constantin Zopounidis, Technical University of Crete

This special issue seeks papers that integrate multiple objective programming, goal programming, and artificial intelligence to address complex decision-making in economic and social sciences. The issue welcomes both substantially extended papers from the 16th International Conference on Multiple Objective Programming and Goal Programming (MOPGP'25) held in Varese, Italy, and original work not previously presented at the conference.

Multiple objective optimization and goal programming provide structured frameworks for evaluating conflicting objectives, while artificial intelligence enhances these approaches through data analytics and machine learning. The combination enables processing of large datasets and improves the accuracy and robustness of decision models and predictions in addressing real-world challenges.

item.title: OR for Sustainability in Supply Chain Management
item.content:encoded:
Kannan Govindan, University of Southern Denmark

Organizations must align operations with UN sustainable development goals to address resource depletion and environmental degradation. This special section seeks research using operations research methods to implement SDGs in supply chain management, particularly advanced optimization techniques like multi-attribute and multi-objective decision-making.

The section invites contributions on three themes: designing sustainable policies with stakeholder involvement, implementing SDGs through innovative supply chain practices, and monitoring progress toward sustainability targets in supply chain governance. Research should examine how organizations balance economic growth with resource conservation and environmental protection.

The collection welcomes interdisciplinary approaches integrating environmental, economic, and social perspectives. Submissions should demonstrate how operations research and optimization algorithms support data-driven decisions that achieve sustainable development goals while improving organizational efficiency and human wellbeing.

item.title: OR in Medicine and Health Care
item.content:encoded:
Eva K. Lee, Georgia Institute of Technology

Ariela Sofer, George Mason University

This special section seeks contributions applying optimization and computational methods to medical and healthcare challenges. The collection welcomes theoretical and methodological work on models and algorithms including continuous linear and nonlinear optimization, integer programming, combinatorial optimization, and stochastic approaches applied to medical and biological problems. Applications span disease modeling, diagnosis, treatment planning, imaging, epidemiology, and molecular biology.

The partnership between mathematical programming researchers and medical professionals—clinicians, biologists, public health officials—creates opportunities to advance both optimization theory and practice while addressing important healthcare problems. The special section, established in 2000, publishes state-of-the-art research in this dynamic field on an ongoing basis.

Original, previously unpublished manuscripts submitted to this collection are evaluated through standard peer review by the Annals of Operations Research.
